rack_room.name: Rack Room
rack_room.description: ONE EQUIPMENT RACK AT WALK-UP SCALE, and five conditions of what it admits exists behind its own controls. 1.12 m wide, 1.60 m tall, on a 1.30 x 0.74 m floor tile: sixteen bay positions on a real rack grid (two columns of 19-inch panel width, eight rows of 4U), five of which carry bare controls - a master knob pair, a screen with two knobs, an 18-way patch field, a four-fader bank with a meter, a six-knob row. The controls are identical at every value of the axis. none leaves nothing behind them. plate puts one dark panel across both columns with a lip and a lit foot strip. vacancy adds a blanking cover over every position no control occupies, merged along each row, screwed down in lighter metal - and leaves ONE BAY OPEN: a 0.44 x 0.15 m hole with 0.47 m of cavity behind it, punched rails, a connector, and four empty screw holes in the jamb where its cover went. frame strips the panel to four uprights, eight cross members and four punched rack strips with the room visible through the middle. works strips it to boards on standoffs, component blocks, a wiring spine, a transformer and a heatsink. THERE IS NO AUDIO IN THIS ARTIFACT AT ANY VALUE - no player, no generator, no bus, no sound_type, no synthesis - and no interaction: it is BoxMesh and StandardMaterial3D throughout. It is a room about the RACK.
dev_themes: what a machine shows of its own insides
interactions: count the positions, then count the ones that hold anything
at vacancy, look into the open bay and find the four empty screw holes beside it
compare frame and works: one shows you how much space the machine occupies, the other shows you what is in it and loses the boundary
rack_room.capacity: SEE that `machinery` is not a scale from closed to open. Ordered by how much of the machine is visible it runs none - plate - vacancy - frame - works, and on that reading `vacancy` is the third of five and unremarkable. Ordered by what the rack can say about what is NOT there, only one value can say anything at all.
rack_room.qfep_connection: The rack is a format before it is an instrument: a grid of positions that exists prior to anything being fitted into it, and that goes on describing what belongs there when nothing does. `vacancy` is the value where the format speaks without a body in it - ten closed positions and one open one, all of them shaped like a module and none of them being one. The other four values can only talk about what the machine HAS.
rack_room.relationships:
Synthesised from the nine registry tokens that declare a `machinery` axis, all of which were read - code, registry entry and doc block.

ONE SCENE, MANY NAMES - CONFIRMED, and it is seven of the nine. [[Rack303Acid]], [[Rack808Drums]], [[RackAmbientDrone]], [[RackDX7Piano]], [[RackMario]], [[RackMoogBass]] and [[RackSineBasic]] are seven .tscn files in commons/audio/rack_presets/ whose ROOT node carries the same one line, `script = ExtResource` pointing at res://addons/element_editor/element_layout_node.gd, with subset_id "audio_rack". They differ only in their `placements` array and their `sound_type` string. So the family is nine NAMES over THREE bodies: that script (7), [[MarioSoundController]] (1) and [[timbre_sculptor]] (1). The tell was not export counts here but file size - seven scenes of 1.0-2.9 KB with one ext_resource between them.

[[MarioSoundController]] is the honest adopter and says so in its own doc block: 'Adopted word for word from the seven promoted audio racks ... because this is the same claim pointed at a different interface: a 3D mapping volume instead of a panel of sliders.' It re-implements all five builders against a ValueMapper3D instead of a cell grid, and carries a transcribed copy of the value list. [[timbre_sculptor]] adds a second axis (`waveform`) and takes `machinery` unchanged, noting in its own registry entry that 'the SOUND is invisible to a still and no axis here pretends otherwise'.

[[warning_yard]] is the pattern this follows: a family word taken off a 1 m body and given a place, with the vocabulary preloaded from the owning member rather than retyped, and the whole argument in the geometry that only the larger scale can hold.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: 1.30 x 0.74 m at the floor tile, so a 2 x 1 patch. wall_backing is FALSE ON PURPOSE and it is not a shrug: at `frame` the whole claim is that the room shows straight through where a panel would be, and at `works` you are meant to read the boards against something. A rack pushed against a wall photographs `frame` as a wall with bars on it. The front is +Z; the token needs a rotation if the approach is not from there. Nothing here is a collider.

measurements.measured_source: computed from the geometry, not from a Godot AABB probe - no Godot was run by the agent that built this. The union across all five values is TILE_W x rack_y1 x TILE_D and its X and Z are set by the constant floor tile: EXT_W 1.1212 < TILE_W 1.30, frontmost control face 0.330 < 0.37, rearmost body -0.280 > -0.37.

dna.default:
machinery=vacancy. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so nothing is being preserved and the default is a free design choice; doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md's rule that outranks everything is about promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was spent on the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest, and `none` - which all nine family members ship as their default, because for them it is the legacy lineage that must not move - is exactly the emptiest.

WHY VACANCY. It is the only value on this axis that can state an ABSENCE. Ordered by how much of the machine you are shown, the five run none - plate - vacancy - frame - works, and vacancy is a middling third. Ordered by what the rack can tell you about what is NOT in it, only vacancy says anything: `works` shows you the most machine and has no vocabulary at all for a part that was never fitted, because a circuit does not have positions; `frame` shows you empty SPACE, which is not the same as an empty PLACE; `plate` and `none` show you nothing about capacity in either direction. Ten covered positions and one open one are eleven statements about a module that is not there, and they are the only such statements the axis can make. A visitor who meets only the default therefore meets the axis's whole argument; a visitor who meets `none` meets a handful of knobs floating over a floor tile and no question.

THE OBJECTION, ANSWERED. At `vacancy` the rack is mostly shut, so a default tile shows less machine than three of the other four values. That is the point rather than a cost: the thing being shown is the FORMAT, and a format is most visible when it is empty.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched; not one line of the nine members' code or registry entries was edited by this pass. This is the cross-member argument those nine leave implicit, built as a body.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE ROOM MAKES, and no member can make it, because it needs a bay you can see into.

Every one of the nine is a bench rack about 0.95 x 0.63 m whose machinery is drawn on a 0.08 m cell grid. On that grid a blanking cover is a 74 mm plate and an unoccupied cell is 80 mm across with nothing behind it, so `vacancy` can only ever mean CLOSED: the family's own builder covers every free cell, and that is the correct choice at that size, because there is nothing to look into. Put the same five words on a 19-inch panel with 0.47 m of depth behind it and the third value acquires a second half it never had: an uncovered position is a cavity with rails down it, a connector at the back and four empty screw holes in the jamb. That is what this room is for, and it is the ONE departure from the family's builder - the covers are all still there, ten of them over eleven free positions, and the eleventh is open.

SO THE ROW TURNS. Ordered by how much of the machine is visible: none - plate - vacancy - frame - works. Ordered by what the rack can say about what is missing: everything ties at nothing except vacancy. Those two orders disagree at the top, and that disagreement is the whole reason `vacancy` is worth building rather than being read as a decorated `plate`.

WHAT EACH VALUE LETS YOU KNOW ABOUT THE MACHINE'S EXTENT, which is the reading the bench cannot stage: `none` - there is no extent, the machine is the parameters. `plate` - you learn its FRONT and nothing else; the depth behind it is unknown and that is the value's entire content. `vacancy` - you learn its CAPACITY, and it is the only value that says a NUMBER: sixteen positions, five used. `frame` - you learn its VOLUME, because the uprights bound a box and the room shows through it, so you can see how much of the machine is empty space. `works` - you learn its CONTENTS and lose the boundary: with no panel there is no edge, and where the machine stops becomes a question about where the wires go.

THOSE NUMBERS ARE EXECUTABLE. `vacancy` is defended above as the only value that says a NUMBER, and the whole argument rests on sixteen positions, five used, ten covered and one open - so _census_check() counts them at _ready from the same tables that draw the geometry (MODULES, _cover_runs(), OPEN_COL/OPEN_ROW) and push_errors if they do not sum to COLS x ROWS, or if the open bay is also a module position. A count typed into a note cannot fail; this can. sorting_hall counted cells whose value changed as a proxy for work and thereby stated that merge sort is free on sorted input.

AND ONE THING THE PICTURE SAYS THAT THE DESIGN DID NOT INTEND. At `vacancy` the covered positions are the most finished-looking thing in the rack: clean sheet metal, screwed down, straight edges. The occupied positions are bare controls on a dark panel, because the modules deliberately have no faceplates. What this rack has done best is the part of it that does nothing.
dna.kin:
THE WORD AND ITS FIVE VALUES ARE READ OUT OF THE FAMILY, NOT RETYPED. rack_room.gd opens with `const MACHINERY_SOURCE := preload("res://addons/element_editor/element_layout_node.gd")` and validates against MACHINERY_SOURCE.MACHINERIES at _ready. That file is the owner on every count: it AUTHORED the axis (a 40-line doc block at line 51 is where the five words are defined), it serves SEVEN of the nine tokens from one script, and it preloads nothing, so pulling it in costs no dependency chain - its five load() calls are all runtime. It is git-tracked; checked with `git ls-files`, because a promotion has previously landed inside a gitignored addon. The element_editor plugin is not in project.godot's enabled list, which is irrelevant: class_name registration comes from the project-wide script scan and the seven rack scenes reference the script by path.

GDScript will not build an @export_enum hint from a constant, so the literal list is duplicated exactly once as HINT_VALUES and _assert_vocabulary() push_errors if it ever differs from MACHINERY_SOURCE.MACHINERIES, and again if the standing value is not in that list. _read_metadata_overrides() keeps the standing value on an unrecognised word and push_errors LOUDLY if nothing legal was standing - the science_screen path, where the sweep sets a property the code cannot reach and the whole loop turns into an experiment about a typo.

THE MACHINERY COLOURS ARE THE FAMILY'S BUT ARE A TRANSCRIPTION, said out loud with the lines they came from (element_layout_node.gd 1446-1447, 1454, 1464-1465, 1496-1497, 1519-1522). Unlike warning_yard, which preloads path_block's named WARN_* constants, this family writes its palette as inline Color() literals inside the four builders, so there is nothing to read. Three of its numeric constants ARE reused unchanged and survive the jump from a 0.08 m grid to a 0.483 m panel without scaling, because all three are real rack dimensions rather than bench-relative ones: MACH_PLATE 0.016 m of panel, an 8 mm lip 4 mm behind it, MACH_COVER 0.010 m of proud blanking cover.

ONE GEOMETRY CHANGE FROM THE FAMILY, FOR THE operations_gallery REASON. The family's lip is a full-size box behind the panel that shows only as a rim. At this scale it also stands behind the open bay, and the cavity then photographs as the back of the lip - measured in the Python model, where 4,897 px of the frame came back as lip rather than cavity, before it was fixed. It is now four rails: same colour, same 8 mm, same 4 mm gap, nothing opaque behind the opening. A frame is four rails, not a slab.
declines: THE HERO MOVE - stand all five conditions at once in one frame and vary something else. Refused twice over. First, the family's case is MIXED and this is derived from its code, not its prose: element_layout_node.gd's `match machinery` at line 1428 calls _machinery_plate THEN _machinery_vacancy for "vacancy", and calls neither for "frame" or "works". So plate NESTS inside vacancy while plate, frame and works sit SIDE BY SIDE - one nested pair inside a set of parallel readings, which is operations_gallery's third case. There is no top value for an all-at-once frame to collapse to, and standing plate and vacancy together would just be vacancy. Second, a synthesis whose axis nobody else declares is a new artifact with a borrowed name; the whole point of reusing a family vocabulary is that the nine can be measured against it.

ANY AUDIO AT ALL - a player, a generator, a bus, a sound_type, a spectrum. Refused on the one-still rule, which is the family's own position and not an imposition: eight of the nine members ARE working synthesisers and their axis is deliberately not about sound, and timbre_sculptor's registry entry says in as many words that the sound is invisible to a still and no axis there pretends otherwise. This room is about the RACK. Adding a voice would add a thing the evidence cannot see, and would make a diorama claim to be an instrument.

MODULE FACEPLATES. Every installed module in a real rack has one, and every one of them was left off. A faceplate is a plate; five of them would put `plate` inside `none` and the first step of the axis would then be measuring a panel that was already there. The cost is that the occupied positions read as bare controls on a dark panel - which is exactly what the family's `none` looks like, and is where the note's last paragraph comes from.

COVERING EVERY FREE POSITION, which is literally what _machinery_vacancy does. Declined for one bay left open, on the record: at 0.08 m per cell a cover is the entire statement because there is nothing to see into, and at 0.4426 x 0.1538 m with 0.47 m behind it, keeping every position shut would have photographed `vacancy` as `plate` with lines ruled on it. The ten covers stay, so the family's reading is fully present and comparable; the hole is the part the bench could not hold.

REPAINTING THE LIP TO MAKE IT VISIBLE. Measured, not assumed: the family's lip colour Color(0.075, 0.078, 0.092) renders at luminance 16.7 on the sweep's default rig, and that rig's background renders at 16.8. The rim the `plate` value describes is invisible on this bench. It was kept anyway - it is the family's colour, it reads under a map's lighting, and a measured fact about the family's palette is worth more than the pixels a repaint would buy. Its SHAPE was changed, for occlusion, which is a different question.

AN OmniLight3D, A SECOND EMISSIVE STRIP, OR ANY OTHER CHEAP CONTRAST. A broad even brightening is exactly the change the critic's own subject_fraction note flags as suspect (frame and focus coming out equal is the tell that a difference is uniform), and a value whose evidence is that it lit the room is measuring the light. There is one emissive surface on the machinery, the family's own lit foot strip, and it is on `plate` and `vacancy` only because it is on the family's `plate` only.

WIDENING THE FOUR SUB-GAUGE DETAILS. The cover's 10 mm proud step is 3.04 px, the punched holes in the rack strips 4.26, the works standoffs 4.26 and the heatsink fins 2.19, all under the 5 px floor. Each is a real dimension, each is texture on a mark that is itself 35-52 px, and no part of the axis is measured on any of them - so they are named here and in _gauge_check's docstring rather than fattened. field_room's ruling: if a thing is thin because the thing it describes is thin, say so with numbers and leave it.

ANY MOTION - a fan, a blinking meter, a sliding fader, a rebuild on a timer. There is no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween and no physics in the file, so a capture's settle cannot photograph this artifact half way through anything.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, AND NOT BY HAND. The whole box list below was rebuilt in Python, projected through the sweep's own camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, exact per-pixel ray-plane depth so nothing is occluded by a painter's algorithm), shaded with capture_config_sweep.gd's frozen default rig (background 0.055/0.055/0.070, AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR 0.62/0.65/0.72 at 0.55, key 1.25 at (-42,-35,0), fill 0.45 at (-20,130,0), Godot's FILMIC curve, sRGB out, PIL luminance), and then run through artifact_dna_critic.py's exact metric - crop to the union subject box, resize to 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5% of |dL|.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS plate <-> vacancy, AT 11.77% FOCUS (2.89% frame).

WHY IT IS KNOWN IN ADVANCE: the family's code says so. `vacancy` calls _machinery_plate and then adds covers, so plate and vacancy differ by exactly the covers, their screws and the one opening, while every other pair differs by a whole body. A nested pair is the minimum by construction, not by luck.

THE ARITHMETIC. dna.framing 0.58 on the union box (radius 1.09605) puts the camera 3.9507 m out, where the visible frame is 2.41569 m across at 314.61 px/m - a square frame of 5.8356 m2. Six cover runs over ten positions present 0.85247 m2 of panel face; at this standpoint a front face keeps cos(0.62) x cos(0.26) = 0.78652, so 0.67049 m2 of screen = 11.49% of the frame, changing from shell luminance 33.7 to cover luminance 57.1, a step of 23.4 grey levels. Add 28 screws at 0.29% of frame and a step of 57.8, the open bay's cavity at 0.71% and a step of about 28, and the two inner rails at 0.06%. Total 80,475 changed pixels of the 577,600 in the tile = 13.93%, mean |dL| over them 24.3. Because the changed area is far above the hottest-5% cut, focus is set by the top of that distribution - the screws, the cavity edges and the cover-to-panel steps - and lands at 11.77%.

THE FALSIFIABLE PART IS THE GAP, NOT THE NUMBER. Runner-up is none <-> plate at 15.87%, only 1.35x larger, and that is far tighter than warning_yard's 2.0x. If the sweep returns none <-> plate as the smallest pair instead, the cause is named in advance and it is SHADOWS: this model has none, and a blanking cover standing 10 mm proud of the panel casts a hard line under all six of its runs in the real render, which adds contrast to plate <-> vacancy and to nothing else. So the model is biased LOW on exactly the pair it is calling closest, and the honest reading of a flip is 'the prediction was right about the mechanism and wrong about which of two effects wins'.

EVERY PAIR, PREDICTED (focus): plate-vacancy 11.77, none-plate 15.87, none-frame 20.21, frame-works 22.02, none-vacancy 23.03, plate-frame 24.08, vacancy-frame 24.38, none-works 24.69, plate-works 27.87, vacancy-works 28.09. MEAN 22.20% -> PREDICTED VERDICT: BITES. No pair is anywhere near the 6% twin bar, and none is predicted identical: the five bodies are geometrically disjoint apart from the one nesting.

KNOWN BIASES OF THE MODEL, so a disagreement can be attributed. It has no shadows, no specular, no ambient occlusion and flat per-face Lambert, and it draws the round controls as boxes - the last of which cannot affect any pair, because the controls are constant and cancel in every diff. All three of the missing terms ADD local contrast, so the real focus numbers should run HIGHER than these across the board; the ORDER is the claim.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL FIVE VALUES, and the union is set by CONSTANT geometry in two of its three axes, which is the point. Union 1.30 x 1.6024 x 0.74: X and Z are the floor tile, which is present at every value, and Y is the rack head, which is present at plate, vacancy, frame and works and exceeded by nothing. The three inequalities that make it true - EXT_W 1.1212 < TILE_W 1.30, frontmost control face 0.330 < TILE_D/2 = 0.37, rearmost body -0.280 > -0.37 - are written into _solve()'s comment. So no value of the axis can move the camera even in principle, which is the trap dna_specimen fell into from the other side.

THE ARITHMETIC. Diagonal sqrt(1.69 + 2.5677 + 0.5476) = 2.19210, radius 1.09605. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would put the camera at 6.8115 m and show a 4.16 m frame - PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, and a 1.6 m object in a 4.16 m frame is 38% of it.

AT 0.58 the camera comes to 3.9507 m and the frame to 2.41569 m, i.e. 314.61 px per metre on a 760 px tile. Projecting the eight corners of the union box through the actual perspective camera, the object spans 65.0% of frame width and 79.6% of frame height, with its worst corner at 0.89 of the half-frame - an 11% margin, which is the reason 0.58 was chosen over 0.55 (94% of the half-frame, a 6% margin, and one bad assumption from a crop). Predicted subject share runs 8.2% at `none` to 23.9% at `plate`; the max across values is what artifact_dna_critic.py uses, so the blank-render check sees 23.9% against its 0.2% bar. `none` is SUPPOSED to be the sparse one - it is the value that says there is no machine.

GAUGE AT 314.61 px/m, AND IT IS EXECUTABLE. _gauge_check() runs at _ready off _g["px_per_m"] - the same single copy of the arithmetic every builder reads, computed from TILE_W, rack_y1, TILE_D, PAD and DNA_FRAMING rather than quoted - and push_warnings any mark under 5.0 px. Seventeen marks are checked, classified by which way the read dimension runs: "s" standing x cos(14.90) = 0.9664, "w" across x sin(0.62) = 0.5810 (the worse of the two horizontal runs, never credited with the yaw's diagonal widening), "d" into the view x sin(14.90) = 0.2571. They run 5.49 to 80.9 px: works side post 5.49, cover screw 6.08, works spine 6.58, rack strip 7.68, works component and works loom 7.90, lit foot strip 9.12, corner upright and lip side rail 9.51, cross member 15.81, lip head rail 22.81, heatsink block 35.10, open bay height 46.76, works board 51.02, transformer 51.69, cover run 52.23, open bay width 80.91. The works side post was 0.020 m and 3.66 px until this check was written and run, and 0.030 m is still an honest rack post.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no audio node and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is ungated and builds the floor, all five control clusters and the machinery body standalone, so nothing has to be supplied for a still and the sweep's rescue path (apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire. The fader levels and the component-block positions are fixed tables, not draws. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE SWEEP SETS THE @export DIRECTLY BEFORE add_child, the grid sets config_machinery metadata, and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary; all three land on the same _read_metadata_overrides. apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY the machinery host and ONLY when the word actually changed and _ready has already built once - the force_pad trap, and a live one here, because curation_station calls apply_grid_config({"emissive": false}) on everything it mounts and that is how all seven promoted racks are placed today.

MEASURE UNSTAGED. This is a 1.6 m floor-standing object with its own floor tile; a --staged run would put a plinth under a thing that already has ground contact and grow the pair AABB, and the union in X and Z would stop being constant.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE, by construction: the floor tile and 76 meshes of controls - the master knob pair with its two buttons, the screen with two knobs, eighteen jacks, four faders with an eight-segment meter, six knobs. That is 8.2% of the frame that cannot move, and it is what makes the five tiles a comparison rather than five pictures. Anything that changes between tiles is machinery.

STRONGEST PAIRS, predicted: anything against `works`, because works is the only value that puts the frame's brightest large surfaces (standoffs and spine at luminance 84, wiring at 108) in the middle of the picture while removing the panel behind them. vacancy-works at 28.09% is the maximum.

WEAKEST PAIR: plate against vacancy, at a predicted 11.77%, and it is weak for a reason that is a finding rather than a fault. The family's own palette puts a blanking cover (albedo 0.215) on a shell (albedo 0.125): 11.5% of the frame changes, but by only 23 grey levels, because a rack is a dark object with slightly less dark panels bolted to it. THE MOST IMPORTANT VALUE ON THIS AXIS IS ALSO ITS QUIETEST STEP. If that comes back under the critic's 12% WEAK bar it is not evidence that `vacancy` is decoration - the axis is judged on the mean of ten pairs, predicted 22.20% - it is evidence about how little contrast the family gave itself between a panel and the thing you bolt over a hole in it.

AND THE HONEST WARNING ABOUT THE OPEN BAY: it is 0.71% of the frame. The single most important object in this artifact - the empty bay that the whole room was built to photograph - is under one percent of the tile, because a bay is one sixteenth of a rack and a rack seen at 3.95 m is not large. Its two dimensions are 46.76 and 80.91 px, so it is legible; it is just small. Do not read a modest plate-vacancy number as the hole failing to render. Look at the PNG: at `vacancy` there is a black rectangle in the left column, fourth row, with a lit rail down its far side and four dark dots in the jamb beside it.
